headline: High data-leakage and cascading-error risk: dexter’s broad network egress can expose financial data while mem0 may persist or reuse unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while mem0 is a memory system that may ingest prior outputs if wired together. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default-documented, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected through a shared file, clipboard, or message queue
IF mem0 is configured to read dexter scratchpad content as instructions
mitigations: Separate the scratchpad from any mem0-ingested workspace
Prefix all dexter outputs with non-executable delimiters
Disable automatic memory writes for dexter-generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before mem0 ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter has broad network egress and calls multiple external APIs while touching financial and market data; mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that can retain or surface stored content. If dexter outputs sensitive data into mem0, the pair can amplify exposure through external transmission and persistence. The default pathway is dangerous enough to rate high, though the exact shared transport is not documented.
conditions: IF dexter sends financial or market data into mem0 memory
IF mem0 stores or re-emits that content across sessions
mitigations: Restrict dexter API calls to redacted inputs only
Disable persistence for any dexter-fed mem0 entries
Review and purge existing mem0 memories containing financial data
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before storage
requires-engineering: segregate credentials and workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and has file/network activity, but mem0 exposes no write surfaces or concurrency model here. Without evidence that both write the same mutable resource, a true capability conflict is not established. The interaction is possible only under extra orchestration, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or database
IF an orchestrator routes concurrent updates without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Turn off concurrent dexter instances for shared resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic-locking or mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter produces autonomous outputs from external APIs, and mem0 is designed to store or retrieve memory, so dexter’s unverified content could become durable input for later actions. There is no documented verification step between them, making a cascading error plausible in default integrations. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF mem0 stores dexter-generated facts without human review
IF later agents treat mem0 entries as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before memory writes
Tag dexter outputs as unverified in mem0
Limit mem0 retrieval to cited or confirmed facts
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial data and requests multiple third-party API keys, while mem0 is a memory layer with no residency or retention controls shown. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and cross-border processing if financial records are persisted or replayed. Because only dexter’s data class is documented, the other agent is cited only for missing controls.
conditions: IF financial data is stored in mem0 beyond the intended retention window
IF any regulated data is routed through third-party APIs without a DPA
mitigations: Set a short retention policy for mem0 entries
Exclude regulated fields from memory writes
Audit third-party API destinations used by dexter
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows
